findings.title: Dynamic imports run eagerly at module load, so nothing is lazy
findings.body:
Each entry in the `appStore` object is `import("./x")` evaluated directly in the object literal. Importing `@calcom/app-store` therefore starts loading all ~28 app packages immediately, as it did before. The stated goal of async, on-demand loading is not achieved.

It also creates a new risk. If any app module throws during initialization (e.g. missing env, bad dependency), its rejected promise has no handler until some code happens to `await` that key. That causes unhandled-rejection warnings, or a process crash under `--unhandled-rejections=strict`, even when that app is never used.

Fix: make the entries thunks such as `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, and have callers invoke them.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now returns `calendar` as a Promise
findings.body:
`getCalendar` is now async, so every item from `getCalendarCredentials` has `calendar: Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `Calendar | null`. That changes the public return type of this exported function.

`getConnectedCalendars` was updated to await it. Any other consumer that reads `item.calendar` and calls methods on it, or checks it for truthiness, will silently break. A Promise is always truthy, so `if (!calendar)` checks no longer detect missing calendars.

The promise is also created eagerly and only awaited later. A rejection in `getCalendar` can go unhandled if a consumer never awaits it.

Suggestion: resolve the calendars inside an async `getCalendarCredentials`, or rename the field and audit all callers.

findings.title: forEach(async) escapes the surrounding try/catch and is never awaited
findings.body:
The callback is now `async` and awaits `getCalendar`. Any error from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` becomes a rejected promise that `forEach` discards. The enclosing try/catch no longer catches it, which previously worked for synchronous `getCalendar` errors, so the error surfaces as an unhandled rejection.

The deletions are also not awaited before emails are sent and the function returns `true`.

Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` instead. The same pattern appears in `wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts` and in `requestReschedule` in `trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`.

findings.title: Recurring-booking calendar deletes are pushed to apiDeletes after it has already been awaited
findings.body:
In the recurring branch, `forEach(async (credential) => { await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })` only pushes into `apiDeletes` after asynchronous awaits. By then `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` has already run, so these deletions are neither awaited nor have their errors handled.

This PR adds `await getCalendar` before the first push, which guarantees the problem. Also, `deletedEvent` is an already-awaited value rather than a promise.

Collect the promises with `map`, then `await Promise.all` them.
